mainTopic: The decrees on non-Jews' bread, oil, wine and daughters: their link to עבודה זרה, the layers of the bans on relations and ייחוד, and the impurity of a non-Jewish boy.
overview: The גמרא first finishes a source from a פסוק in מלאכי: a decree needs the acceptance of 'the whole nation.' It then goes back to רב's statement that the bans on non-Jews' bread, oil, wine and daughters belong to the י״ח דבר. The decree about 'daughters' means non-Jewish girls are treated as נידות from the cradle. A second report says all these decrees were made because of עבודה זרה, in a chain: bread and oil because of wine, wine because of daughters, and daughters because of עבודה זרה. The גמרא then asks what the decree on daughters added beyond the תורה. Each answer it gives is pushed back by an earlier source: the court of שם, a הלכה למשה מסיני, the court of the חשמונאים, and the court of דוד. In the end it sorts out layers of the ייחוד ban: a married woman (תורה), an unmarried woman (דוד), and a non-Jewish woman (students of שמאי and הלל). Last, it explains the final link: a non-Jewish boy was made impure like a זב to prevent משכב זכור. A story about רבי shows this impurity starts at nine years and one day.

steps.title: A verse shows a decree needs the whole nation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the פסוק from מלאכי and learns from it that a decree needs the acceptance of the whole nation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'You are cursed with the curse, yet you rob Me, even this whole nation.' This teaches: if the whole nation is involved, yes; if not, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up an earlier discussion by bringing the פסוק that serves as its source. From the words 'the whole nation' it learns that a decree takes hold only when the whole nation accepts it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key words are 'הגוי כולו', 'the whole nation.' The verse speaks of a curse that falls on the people when 'the whole nation' is involved. The גמרא reads this as a rule: a decree takes hold only if the people as a whole accept it, and not otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: Robbing / taking what belongs to someone else (in this verse)

phrases.english: "You are cursed with the curse,
phrases.notes: מלאכי 3:9

phrases.english: yet you rob Me,
even this whole nation."
If there is the whole nation, yes;
phrases.notes: He means: if the whole nation accepts the decree, it takes hold.

phrases.english: if not, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמְּאֵרָה אַתֶּם נֵאָרִים וְאֹתִי אַתֶּם קֹבְעִים הַגּוֹי כֻּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the source-search from the discussion that came just before this text.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a decree takes hold only with the acceptance of the whole nation.

steps.title: Bread, oil, wine and daughters are part of the eighteen decrees
steps.stepSummary: באלי quotes אבימי of Nota, in the name of רב: the bans on non-Jews' bread, oil, wine and daughters all belong to the eighteen decrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the statement itself: באלי said in the name of אבימי of Nota, quoting רב: their bread, their oil, their wine and their daughters are all among the eighteen decrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a statement it quoted earlier ('גופא') and now looks at it in detail. רב says these four bans are all part of the famous group of eighteen decrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The י״ח דבר were eighteen decrees made on one day by the students of שמאי and הלל. Saying these four bans belong to that group tells us when and by whom they were made. It also gives them the strength of that famous group of decrees.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': going back to look closely at a statement quoted earlier
The eighteen decrees made on one day by the students of שמאי and הלל

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether these bans are part of the י״ח דבר matters because those decrees are especially firm.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Balei says
that Avimi of Nota says in the name of Rav:
Their bread and their oil,
their wine and their daughters,
all of them are from the eighteen matters.
phrases.notes: These are the eighteen decrees made in one day by the students of שמאי and הלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר בָּאלִי אָמַר אֲבִימִי נִוְתָאָה מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion by going back to a statement quoted earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bans on non-Jews' bread, oil, wine and daughters all belong to the י״ח דבר.

steps.title: What was the decree about their daughters?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the decree about 'their daughters' actually was.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their daughters: what is that decree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. Bread, oil and wine are easy to picture, but what was decreed about 'daughters'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Marrying non-Jews is already forbidden by the תורה. So a decree about 'their daughters' must add something new, and the גמרא wants to know what that is. This question sets up the answer in the next step.

phrases.english: Their daughters: what is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנוֹתֵיהֶן מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what one item in רב's list means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly was decreed about non-Jews' daughters.

steps.title: They are treated as נידות from the cradle
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains: the decree was that non-Jewish girls are treated as נידות from the time they are in the cradle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: they decreed that their daughters are considered נידות from their cradles.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the question. The decree was to treat non-Jewish girls as נידות from the time they are babies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a girl is not a נידה until she has her first period. This decree treats non-Jewish girls as נידות all the time, starting from babyhood. That is the new thing the decree added.

keyTerms.meaning: Women in the state of נידה (ritually impure from menstruation)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about whether marriage to a non-Jew is allowed. That is already forbidden. The decree adds the law of נידה, starting even from babyhood.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak says:
They decreed upon their daughters
that they are menstruating women from their cradles.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק גָּזְרוּ עַל בְּנוֹתֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Non-Jewish girls are treated as נידות from the time they are in the cradle.
steps.whatToRemember: According to באלי, all four bans are part of the י״ח דבר, and 'their daughters' means they are treated as נידות from the cradle.

steps.title: A second view: all four were decreed because of עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: גניבא, in the name of רב, says that all four bans were made because of עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And גניבא said in the name of רב: all of them were decreed because of עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of what רב said. גניבא says the reason behind all four decrees was to keep Jews away from עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: באלי's report was about which group the decrees belong to. גניבא's report gives the reason for them: they are all protective fences around עבודה זרה. The next steps will show how each decree leads to the next.

phrases.english: And Geneiva says in the name of Rav:
All of them, because of idol worship,
they decreed upon them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּגְנִיבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different report of רב's view on the same four decrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All four decrees were made to keep Jews away from עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Support from רבי יצחק: bread was banned because of oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports גניבא with a teaching of רבי יצחק, brought by רב אחא בר אדא, that the decrees were linked one to another: bread was banned because of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: For when רב אחא בר אדא came, he said in the name of רבי יצחק: they decreed on their bread because of their oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching to back up גניבא. רבי יצחק says one decree was made to protect another, starting with bread being banned because of oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'דכי' ('for when') shows this is brought as support. If the decrees form a chain, each guarding the next, then the chain can lead back to עבודה זרה, just as גניבא said. This version of the teaching, though, will be questioned right away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For when he came': introduces a teaching brought from ארץ ישראל to בבל

phrases.aramaic: דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא
phrases.english: As, when Rav Acha bar Adda came,
he said that Rabbi Yitzchak says:
They decreed upon their bread because of their oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for גניבא's view.
steps.raayaObject: גניבא's view that the decrees are linked and lead back to עבודה זרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יצחק, as brought by רב אחא בר אדא.

steps.title: Why would oil be more serious than bread?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording: why would oil be a bigger worry than bread, so that bread is banned to protect oil?
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes oil stronger than bread?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק's wording. Bread and oil seem to be on the same level, so why would one be banned to protect the other?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A protective decree makes sense only when it guards something more serious. Nothing makes oil more serious than bread. So 'bread because of oil' does not work as a chain.

phrases.english: What is the strength of oil over bread?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אוּלְמֵיהּ דְּשֶׁמֶן מִפַּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the teaching quoted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's statement that bread was banned because of oil.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A protective decree must guard something more serious. Oil is not more serious than bread, so the link makes no sense.

steps.title: The correct chain: bread and oil, then wine, then daughters, then עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the teaching: bread and oil were banned because of wine, wine because of daughters, daughters because of עבודה זרה, and one more link follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: they decreed on their bread and oil because of their wine, on their wine because of their daughters, on their daughters because of 'something else' (עבודה זרה), and on 'something else' because of 'something else.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of רבי יצחק's teaching. Bread and oil together protect against wine, wine protects against marrying their daughters, and that protects against עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now each link guards something more serious than itself, and the chain ends at עבודה זרה. That fits גניבא's view well. The last phrase adds one more link, which the גמרא explains later, in steps 27–28, after its long discussion of the ban on daughters.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Something else': a polite way of referring to עבודה זרה

steps.whatToRemember: According to גניבא's view, the decrees form a chain: bread and oil, then wine, then daughters, then עבודה זרה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'דבר אחר' here is not 'another explanation.' It is a polite name for עבודה זרה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, עַל פִּיתָּן וְשַׁמְנָן מִשּׁוּם יֵינָן,
phrases.english: Rather, upon their bread and their oil because of their wine,
and upon their wine because of their daughters,
phrases.notes: Drinking together leads to closeness, and that can lead to marrying their daughters.

phrases.english: and upon their daughters because of something else,
phrases.notes: 'Something else' is a polite way of saying עבודה זרה.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל דָּבָר אַחֵר מִשּׁוּם דָּבָר אַחֵר.
phrases.english: and upon something else because of something else.
phrases.notes: The גמרא explains this last link later, in steps 27–28.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, עַל פִּיתָּן וְשַׁמְנָן מִשּׁוּם יֵינָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by correcting the wording of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the quoted teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bread was banned to protect oil.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bread and oil were banned to protect wine, wine to protect daughters, and daughters to protect against עבודה זרה, with one more link still to be explained.

steps.title: Isn't the ban on their daughters already from the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the ban on non-Jewish daughters was a rabbinic decree, because the Torah already says 'Do not marry with them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Their daughters? That is already a Torah law, as it says: 'Do not marry with them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the list of decrees from step 8. How can the rabbis decree something the Torah already forbids?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rabbinic decree is meant to add something new. If the תורה already forbids marrying non-Jews, then calling the ban on 'their daughters' a decree makes no sense. The גמרא must find what the decree added beyond the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Their daughters (marrying or being with non-Jewish women)
From the Torah itself, not a rabbinic rule

phrases.english: Their daughters? That is a Torah law!
As it is written: "Do not marry with them."
phrases.notes: דברים 7:3

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנוֹתֵיהֶן, דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the item 'daughters' in the list of decrees from step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ban on non-Jewish daughters is a rabbinic decree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק already forbids intermarriage, so there would be nothing left for the rabbis to decree

steps.title: The Torah covers only the seven nations
steps.stepSummary: The Torah ban covers only the seven Canaanite nations; the rabbis extended it to all other nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: By Torah law, only the seven nations are forbidden, but not other nations. They came and decreed even about other nations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The פסוק is about the seven nations only, and the decree added everyone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'Do not marry with them' is read narrowly, as talking about the seven nations of כנען. That leaves room for a real decree. The rabbis forbade marrying people of any other nation too.

keyTerms.meaning: The other nations of the world

phrases.english: By Torah law, it is only the seven nations,
but the other nations, no,
and they came and decreed
phrases.notes: "They" are the rabbis who made these decrees, the students of שמאי and הלל.

phrases.english: even about the other nations.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא שִׁבְעָה גּוֹיִם, אֲבָל שְׁאָר אוּמּוֹת לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the Torah law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק forbids all non-Jews, so there is nothing left to decree
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah covers the seven nations; the decree added all other nations

steps.title: But רבי שמעון בן יוחי says the Torah covers all nations
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי שמעון בן יוחי, the next פסוק extends the Torah ban to all nations, so the previous answer doesn't work for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי שמעון בן יוחי, who says 'For he will turn your son away from Me' comes to include all who turn away, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 10. One תנא reads the Torah ban as covering every nation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן יוחי looks at the reason the תורה gives: they will turn your son away. That reason applies to any non-Jew, not only the seven nations. So for him the Torah already forbids all nations, and the 'other nations' answer fails.

keyTerms.meaning: For he will turn your son away from Me
To include all who turn away
What is there to say? (the answer doesn't work)

phrases.english: And according to רבי שמעון בן יוחי, who says:
"For he will turn your son away from Me"
phrases.notes: דברים 7:4

phrases.english: comes to include all who turn away,
phrases.notes: He means any non-Jew who might pull your son away, not just the seven nations.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 10 using another תנא's reading
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the Torah ban covers only the seven nations
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי שמעון בן יוחי the Torah covers every nation, so the decree would add nothing

steps.title: The Torah forbids marriage; the rabbis added casual relations
steps.stepSummary: The Torah forbids relations through marriage; the rabbis added relations outside of marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, by Torah law it is relations by way of marriage, and they came and decreed even by way of promiscuity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer that works even for רבי שמעון בן יוחי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new line is not about which nations but about what kind of relationship. The פסוק talks about marrying, so it forbids only married relations. The decree added casual relations with non-Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: By way of promiscuity, outside marriage

phrases.english: Rather, by Torah law it is relations by way of marriage,
and they came and decreed
even by way of promiscuity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא אִישׁוּת דֶּרֶךְ חַתְנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer of step 10 with a new one
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the line between Torah law and the decree by type of relationship
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree was about nations not covered by the Torah
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah forbids married relations; the decree added casual relations

steps.title: Casual relations were already banned by the court of שם
steps.stepSummary: Casual relations were already forbidden long before, by the court of שם, as seen when יהודה ordered תמר burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Promiscuity too was decreed already in the court of שם, as it is written: 'And יהודה said: Take her out and let her be burned!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 12. The 'new' decree on casual relations was not new at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יהודה heard that תמר had been with a man outside marriage, he ordered her burned. That shows a ban on casual relations already existed in the court of שם. So the later rabbis could not have been the first to decree it.

keyTerms.meaning: The court of שם, son of נח
Take her out and let her be burned

phrases.english: Promiscuity too
was decreed in the court of שם,
as it is written: "And יהודה said:
Take her out and let her be burned!"
phrases.notes: בראשית 38:24. This is said about תמר.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְנוּת נָמֵי בְּבֵית דִּינוֹ שֶׁל שֵׁם גָּזְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the later rabbis first decreed against casual relations
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק shows that the court of שם already banned it long before

steps.title: The Torah covers a non-Jewish man; the rabbis added a non-Jewish woman
steps.stepSummary: The Torah forbids a non-Jewish man with a Jewish woman, because she gets drawn after him. The rabbis added a Jewish man with a non-Jewish woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, by Torah law it is a non-Jew who is with a Jewish woman, because she is drawn after him. But a Jew who is with a non-Jewish woman is not forbidden by the Torah. They came and decreed even a Jew who is with a non-Jewish woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer: the line is drawn by which side is Jewish. This answer is challenged in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is being pulled after the other person's ways. A Jewish woman with a non-Jewish man is likely to be drawn after him, so that case is forbidden earlier. The new decree covered the opposite case: a Jewish man with a non-Jewish woman.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish man who is with a Jewish woman
Because she is drawn after him
A Jewish man who is with a non-Jewish woman

steps.whatToRemember: At this stage the גמרא says the Torah forbids a non-Jewish man with a Jewish woman, and the decree added a Jewish man with a non-Jewish woman. The next steps narrow this further.

phrases.english: Rather, by Torah law
it is a non-Jew who is with a Jewish woman,
because she is drawn after him;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יִשְׂרָאֵל הַבָּא עַל הַגּוֹיָה — לָא,
phrases.english: but a Jew who is with a non-Jewish woman, not,
and they came and decreed
even about a Jew who is with a non-Jewish woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא גּוֹי הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer of step 12 after the קשיא of step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the line by which side is Jewish
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The decree was about casual relations in general
steps.terutzMaskana: A non-Jewish man with a Jewish woman was already forbidden; the decree added a Jewish man with a non-Jewish woman

steps.title: This ban already comes from Sinai
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 14. A Jewish man with a non-Jewish woman is already a הלכה למשה מסיני, as shown by the rule that קנאין may attack him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Jewish man who has relations with a non-Jewish woman is a law given to משה at סיני. As the Master said: if someone has relations with an Aramean woman, zealots may attack him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 14. You can't say the rabbis added the case of a Jewish man with a non-Jewish woman, because that case was already forbidden from סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 said the Torah only forbids a non-Jewish man with a Jewish woman, and the rabbis added the reverse case. But a הלכה למשה מסיני already forbids the reverse case. The proof is that קנאין are allowed to attack such a man, which shows the act is forbidden at the highest level.

keyTerms.meaning: A law given to משה at סיני by oral tradition, with Torah-level force
One who has relations with an Aramean (non-Jewish) woman

phrases.english: A Jewish man who has relations with a non-Jewish woman
that is a law given to Moses at Sinai,
as the Master said:
one who has relations with an Aramean woman,
zealots may attack him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה לְמֹשֶׁה מִסִּינַי הִיא, דְּאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 14's claim that the rabbis added the ban on a Jewish man with a non-Jewish woman
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That case already has Sinai-level force, because קנאין may attack the man, so the rabbis could not have been the first to add it.

steps.title: Sinai covers public acts; the rabbis added private ones
steps.stepSummary: The Sinai rule applies only to a public act like the story of זמרי. The rabbis extended the ban to acts done in private.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: by Torah law, it is forbidden in public, like the incident that happened. Then they came and decreed that it is forbidden even in private.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer narrows the Sinai rule. It covers only a public act, like what happened with זמרי, and the rabbis added the ban on private acts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about קנאין is real, but it only applies to an act done publicly. So the rabbis still added something new: a ban on the same act in private. This saves the idea that the rabbis made a real new decree here.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the incident that happened (זמרי and the Midianite woman)
They; here, the rabbis whose decree is being discussed

phrases.english: He said to him:
By Torah law, it is forbidden in public,
and like the incident that happened,
phrases.notes: This is the story of זמרי in במדבר 25, which happened in front of everyone.

phrases.english: and they came and decreed
phrases.notes: "They" are the rabbis of the decree we've been talking about, the students of שמאי and הלל.

phrases.english: even in private.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by limiting the Sinai rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope: public versus private
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Sinai rule forbids every case of a Jewish man with a non-Jewish woman, so the rabbis added nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Sinai rule covers only a public act like זמרי's. The rabbis added the ban on private acts.

steps.title: The חשמונאים already banned private acts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: the court of the חשמונאים already banned this act even in private, long before the students of שמאי and הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in private, too, the court of the חשמונאים already made a decree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new answer from step 16. The private case was already banned earlier, by the court of the חשמונאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 said the later rabbis added the ban on private acts. But if the חשמונאים had already banned private acts, the later rabbis added nothing new. The proof for this comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The court of the חשמונאים (the Hasmonean rulers)

phrases.english: In private, too,
the court of the Hasmoneans decreed!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּצִינְעָא נָמֵי בֵּית דִּינוֹ שֶׁל חַשְׁמוֹנַאי גָּזְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 16's claim that the later rabbis first banned private acts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An earlier court, the חשמונאים, had already banned private acts, so the later rabbis would have added nothing new.

steps.title: רב דימי's report of the חשמונאים' decree
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reported that the court of the חשמונאים decreed that a Jewish man with a non-Jewish woman breaks the prohibitions marked by the letters נשג"א.
steps.simpleTranslation: As when רב דימי came, he said: the court of the חשמונאים decreed that a Jewish man who has relations with a non-Jewish woman is liable because of נשג"א.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the proof for the challenge in step 17. רב דימי reports that the court of the חשמונאים made such a decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נשג"א is a memory aid: נדה, שפחה, גויה, אשת איש. The court treated a man with a non-Jewish woman as if he broke all four of these. This shows the חשמונאים had already made a strong decree on this case, with no public setting required.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל to בבל
Memory aid for: a נדה, a maidservant, a non-Jewish woman, a married woman

steps.confusionAlert: נשג"א is not a word. It is four first letters, each standing for a different forbidden woman.

phrases.english: As when Rav Dimi came, he said:
The court of the Hasmoneans decreed
that a Jewish man who has relations with a non-Jewish woman
is liable on account of N-Sh-G-A.
phrases.notes: נדה, שפחה, גויה, אשת איש: he is treated as if he broke all four.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the challenge of step 17
steps.raayaObject: That the court of the חשמונאים already decreed against a Jewish man with a non-Jewish woman
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב דימי's report of the decree (נשג"א)

steps.title: רבין's version: נשג"ז
steps.stepSummary: רבין reported the same decree, but with זונה in place of אשת איש: נשג"ז.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: he is liable because of נשג"ז.
steps.whatsHappening: A second scholar reports the same decree of the חשמונאים, with one letter changed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבין replaces אשת איש with זונה, so the letters stand for נדה, שפחה, גויה, זונה. The details differ, but both reports agree that the חשמונאים made this decree. So the challenge of step 17 still stands either way.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל to בבל
Memory aid for: a נדה, a maidservant, a non-Jewish woman, a זונה

steps.whatToRemember: Two reports, from רב דימי and from רבין, both show that the court of the חשמונאים banned this act even in private. That came before the students of שמאי and הלל, which puts step 16's answer under pressure.

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:
on account of N-Sh-G-Z.
phrases.notes: Same list, but זונה takes the place of אשת איש.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of the report in step 18
steps.raayaObject: That the court of the חשמונאים already made this decree

steps.title: The court of the חשמונאים banned relations, the later rabbis banned being alone
steps.stepSummary: The court of the חשמונאים banned only relations with a non-Jewish woman. The students of שמאי and הלל came later and added a ban on even being alone with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the court of the חשמונאים made its decree, it banned only relations, not being alone. Then the students of שמאי and הלל came and banned even being alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 17. It says the students of שמאי and הלל added something the court of the חשמונאים had not banned: being alone with a non-Jewish woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 asked what the students of שמאי and הלל added if the court of the חשמונאים already banned relations even in private. The answer is that the new rule was about ייחוד, being alone together, which is one step further back from the act itself.

keyTerms.meaning: A man and a woman being alone together in private

phrases.aramaic: כִּי גָּזְרוּ בֵּית דִּינוֹ שֶׁל חַשְׁמוֹנַאי בִּיאָה,
phrases.english: When the court of the Hasmoneans decreed, it was about intercourse,
but about seclusion, no.
And they came and decreed even about seclusion.
phrases.notes: "They" means the students of שמאי and הלל, the ones we are trying to explain.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי גָּזְרוּ בֵּית דִּינוֹ שֶׁל חַשְׁמוֹנַאי בִּיאָה, אֲבָל יִיחוּד לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17, which was backed up by the reports in steps 18 and 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the decrees by subject: relations versus being alone.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the students of שמאי and הלל added nothing, because the court of the חשמונאים had already banned relations in private.
steps.terutzMaskana: The court of the חשמונאים banned relations. The students of שמאי and הלל added a ban on ייחוד.

steps.title: But דוד's court already banned being alone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 20: the ban on ייחוד was already made long before, by the court of דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Being alone together was also banned already, by the court of דוד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. If ייחוד was already banned by דוד's court, the students of שמאי and הלל did not add it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said the new thing was ייחוד. This challenge says ייחוד is not new at all, because it goes back to the court of דוד. The proof comes in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: יִיחוּד נָמֵי בֵּית דִּינוֹ שֶׁל דָּוִד גָּזְרוּ!
phrases.english: Seclusion too, the court of David already decreed against!

steps.triggerLanguage: יִיחוּד נָמֵי בֵּית דִּינוֹ שֶׁל דָּוִד גָּזְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 20 that the students of שמאי and הלל were the first to ban ייחוד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An earlier court, the court of דוד, already banned ייחוד, so it cannot be the new rule of the students of שמאי and הלל.

steps.title: רב יהודה's report that דוד's court banned being alone
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says that at that time, in the days of דוד, they made a decree about ייחוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said: at that time they made a decree about being alone together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that backs up the challenge in step 21.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's statement shows that a ban on ייחוד already existed in the days of דוד. That makes the challenge to step 20 strong.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said:
At that time they decreed about seclusion.
phrases.notes: "That time" means right after the story of אמנון and תמר in שמואל ב 13.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה גָּזְרוּ עַל יִיחוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the challenge of step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That the court of דוד banned ייחוד.

steps.title: דוד's court banned being alone with a Jewish woman only
steps.stepSummary: The court of דוד banned ייחוד only with a Jewish woman. The students of שמאי and הלל extended the ban to a non-Jewish woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answered: there, in דוד's time, the ban was on being alone with a Jewish woman, not with a non-Jewish woman. The students of שמאי and הלל came and banned even being alone with a non-Jewish woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 21 by narrowing what דוד's court banned. That leaves room for the students of שמאי and הלל to add something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the history has three layers. דוד's court banned ייחוד with a Jewish woman, the חשמונאים banned relations with a non-Jewish woman, and the students of שמאי and הלל banned ייחוד with a non-Jewish woman.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three layers of rules. דוד's court banned being alone with a Jewish woman. The court of the חשמונאים banned relations with a non-Jewish woman. The students of שמאי and הלל banned being alone with a non-Jewish woman.

phrases.english: They said:
There, it was seclusion with a Jewish woman,
but seclusion with a gentile woman, no.

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתוֹ אִינְהוּ גְּזַרוּ אֲפִילּוּ אַיִּיחוּד דְּגוֹיָה.
phrases.english: And they came and decreed even about seclusion with a gentile woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָתָם יִיחוּד דְּבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 21 and 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the earlier decree to one type of woman.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought דוד's court banned every kind of ייחוד, so nothing was left for the students of שמאי and הלל to add.
steps.terutzMaskana: דוד's court banned only ייחוד with a Jewish woman. The ban on ייחוד with a non-Jewish woman is the new rule.

steps.title: Being alone with a Jewish woman is already a Torah law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 23: ייחוד with a Jewish woman is a Torah law, so דוד's court could not have been the one to ban it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But being alone with a Jewish woman is forbidden by the Torah itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. If the ban on ייחוד with a Jewish woman comes from the Torah, what did דוד's court decree?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 depended on דוד's court making the ban on ייחוד with a Jewish woman. If the Torah already forbids it, that decree adds nothing, and the whole picture falls apart. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah itself, not a rabbinic decree

phrases.english: Seclusion with a Jewish woman is from the Torah!

steps.triggerLanguage: יִיחוּד דְּבַת יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 23 that דוד's court decreed against ייחוד with a Jewish woman.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic court does not need to decree what the Torah already forbids.

steps.title: The hint for being alone from the verse about the enticing brother
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, finds a Torah hint for ייחוד in the words "your brother, the son of your mother." A son may be alone with his mother, but no one else may be alone with any of the women the Torah forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: where does the Torah hint at the ban on being alone? From the פסוק "If your brother, the son of your mother, entices you." Does only a brother from the same mother entice, and a brother from the same father does not? Rather, the פסוק hints that a son may be alone with his mother, but no one else may be alone with any of the women the Torah forbids.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the Torah source that backs up the challenge in step 24. It reads a small detail in a פסוק as a hint to the ban on ייחוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names a brother from the same mother. The גמרא asks why, since a brother from the same father can entice you too. The answer is that brothers from the same mother spend private time together at their mother's home, because a son may be alone with his mother. This shows that being alone with other forbidden women is not allowed, which means ייחוד is forbidden by the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: A hint, a source in the Torah that is not stated openly
One who entices someone to worship idols
Women the Torah forbids a man to have relations with
Does it really mean that...? It introduces a question about the plain reading

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק is about a person who entices someone to worship idols, not about ייחוד. The גמרא only takes a hint from one small detail in it, the words "son of your mother."
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic Torah source for the ban on ייחוד. It raises the question of what דוד's court could have added if ייחוד is a Torah law. The next step answers this.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
Where is there a hint to seclusion from the Torah?
As it says: "If your brother, the son of your mother, entices you."
phrases.notes: דברים 13:7

phrases.english: Does only the son of a mother entice,
and the son of a father does not entice?
Rather, a son may be alone with his mother,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין אַחֵר מִתְיַיחֵד עִם כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה!
phrases.english: and no one else may be alone with any of the women forbidden in the Torah!
phrases.notes: So ייחוד is already in the Torah, long before דוד. That is the force of the challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק: רֶמֶז לְיִיחוּד מִן הַתּוֹרָה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the Torah source behind the challenge of step 24.
steps.raayaObject: That ייחוד with forbidden women is banned by the Torah.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 13:7, "your brother, the son of your mother," as explained by רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק.

steps.title: Three layers of the ייחוד ban
steps.stepSummary: The Torah forbids ייחוד with a married woman. דוד's court added an unmarried woman, and the students of שמאי and הלל added a non-Jewish woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Being alone with a married woman is forbidden by the Torah. דוד came and banned even being alone with an unmarried woman. Then the students of בית שמאי and בית הלל came and banned even being alone with a non-Jewish woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from steps 24 and 25 by showing that each group banned a different kind of ייחוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah hint from step 25 covers only women the Torah forbids, such as a married woman. So דוד's court really did make something new: a ban on being alone with an unmarried woman. The students of שמאי and הלל then made a third, later layer for a non-Jewish woman.

keyTerms.meaning: from the Torah, a Torah law
made a decree, a rabbinic ban

steps.whatToRemember: ייחוד comes in three layers: married woman (Torah), unmarried woman (דוד's court), non-Jewish woman (students of שמאי and הלל).
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how all three sources from steps 20 to 25 can be true together. Each one added a new layer to the ban.

phrases.english: The Torah-level ban on seclusion is with a married woman,
and דוד came and decreed
even about seclusion with an unmarried woman,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתוֹ תַּלְמִידֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: and the students of בית שמאי and בית הלל came
and decreed even about seclusion with a non-Jewish woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: ייחוד דאורייתא דאשת איש
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 24 by separating the Torah ban from דוד's ban.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: different kinds of women belong to different layers of the law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the Torah already forbids ייחוד, it seemed that דוד's court could not have made a ban.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah ban covers a married woman, דוד added an unmarried woman, and the students of שמאי and הלל added a non-Jewish woman.

steps.title: What does 'something else because of something else' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase 'a decree on something else because of something else' is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'on something else because of something else'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to an earlier phrase about the Rabbis' decrees and asks what it means. This sets up רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'something else' is a polite way of avoiding a sensitive subject, so its meaning is not clear. The גמרא wants to know which decree it refers to and which sin it is meant to prevent.

keyTerms.meaning: 'something else,' a polite way of avoiding naming something unpleasant

phrases.aramaic: מַאי עַל דָּבָר אַחֵר מִשּׁוּם דָּבָר אַחֵר?
phrases.english: What is 'on something else because of something else'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מאי על דבר אחר משום דבר אחר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from ייחוד to explain another phrase from the list of decrees.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which decree the unclear phrase 'on something else because of something else' refers to.

steps.title: A non-Jewish boy is made impure like a זב
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains: the Rabbis made a non-Jewish boy impure like a זב, so that Jewish boys would stay away from him and not come to משכב זכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: They decreed that a non-Jewish boy makes things impure like a זב, so that a Jewish boy will not spend a lot of time with him and come to משכב זכור.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the question from step 27. The decree is about the impurity of a non-Jewish boy, and its purpose is to prevent a forbidden relationship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first 'something else' is the impurity of זיבה that the Rabbis placed on a non-Jewish boy. The second 'something else' is משכב זכור, the sin the decree is meant to prevent. If Jewish boys know he makes them impure, they will keep their distance from him.

keyTerms.meaning: a type of bodily discharge that makes a person impure (a זב)
close with him, spending a lot of time with him

steps.confusionAlert: By the Torah, a non-Jew does not become impure as a זב at all. This impurity exists only because the Rabbis decreed it.

phrases.english: רב נחמן בר יצחק said:
They decreed about a non-Jewish boy
that he makes things impure like a זב,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא תִּינוֹק יִשְׂרָאֵל רָגִיל אֶצְלוֹ
phrases.english: so that a Jewish boy will not be close with him
in a way that leads to משכב זכור.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב נחמן בר יצחק גזרו על תינוק גוי שיטמא בזיבה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The decree is the impurity of זיבה placed on a non-Jewish boy, made to prevent משכב זכור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A non-Jewish boy makes things impure like a זב because of a rabbinic decree.

steps.title: רבי זירא's hard question: from what age?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells how a question passed back through a chain of teachers all the way to רבי: from what age is a non-Jewish boy impure as a זב? רבי said from one day old, but רבי חייא said from nine years and one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: I had great trouble getting an answer from רבי אסי. רבי אסי had the same trouble with רבי יוחנן, רבי יוחנן with רבי ינאי, רבי ינאי with רבי נתן בן עמרם, and רבי נתן בן עמרם with רבי. The question was: from when does a non-Jewish boy make things impure as a זב? רבי told me: from one day old. When I came to רבי חייא, he told me: from nine years and one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to support רב נחמן בר יצחק. It shows that the decree is tied to the age when a boy can have relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nine years and one day is the age when a boy's relations count in halacha. If the impurity starts at that age, it fits רב נחמן's reason, which is to prevent משכב זכור. Here two answers are on the table: one day old (רבי) and nine years and one day (רבי חייא).

keyTerms.meaning: nine years and one day old

phrases.english: As רבי זירא said:

phrases.aramaic: צַעַר גָּדוֹל הָיָה לִי אֵצֶל רַבִּי אַסִּי,
phrases.english: I had great trouble with רבי אסי,
and רבי אסי had it with רבי יוחנן,
and רבי יוחנן with רבי ינאי,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יַנַּאי אֵצֶל רַבִּי נָתָן בֶּן עַמְרָם,
phrases.english: and רבי ינאי with רבי נתן בן עמרם,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי נָתָן בֶּן עַמְרָם אֵצֶל רַבִּי:
phrases.english: and רבי נתן בן עמרם with רבי:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא. From here on, 'me' is the person who asked רבי the question.

phrases.english: From when does a non-Jewish boy make things impure as a זב?
And he told me: from one day old,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁבָּאתִי אֵצֶל רַבִּי חִיָּיא אָמַר לִי:
phrases.english: and when I came to רבי חייא, he told me:
from nine years and one day old.

steps.triggerLanguage: דאמר רבי זירא צער גדול היה לי אצל רבי אסי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 28 with a story about the age when the impurity starts.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's reason: the decree is meant to prevent משכב זכור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי זירא's story about the chain of teachers and רבי חייא's answer of nine years and one day.

steps.title: רבי takes back his answer and accepts רבי חייא's
steps.stepSummary: When רבי heard רבי חייא's answer, he dropped his own view and ruled that the impurity starts at nine years and one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I came back and told my words before רבי, he said to me: Leave my words and hold on to the words of רבי חייא, who said: From when does a non-Jewish boy make things impure as a זב? From nine years and one day.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רבי himself accepting nine years and one day. The sentence continues on the next line of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי takes back 'one day old,' the final age is nine years and one day. That is the age when relations count in halacha, so it supports רב נחמן בר יצחק's reason for the decree.

keyTerms.meaning: leave my words, drop my view

steps.whatToRemember: A non-Jewish boy is impure as a זב from age nine years and one day. That age matches the decree's purpose of preventing משכב זכור.

phrases.english: And when I came and told my words before רבי,
phrases.notes: 'My words' here means what רבי חייא had told him.

phrases.english: he said to me: Leave my words
and hold on to the words of רבי חייא.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: תִּינוֹק גּוֹי אֵימָתַי מְטַמֵּא בְּזִיבָה
phrases.english: who said: from when does a non-Jewish boy make things impure as a זב?
From nine years and one day old,

steps.triggerLanguage: הנח דברי ואחוז דברי רבי חייא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the disagreement from step 29 in favor of רבי חייא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The impurity of a non-Jewish boy as a זב begins at nine years and one day, as רבי חייא said and רבי accepted.
